sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I'm happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Tunisia.
Tunisia is a sunny, historic,
and colorful country in North Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Tunisia?
Tunisia is in North Africa.
It is next to Algeria and Libya.
To the North, it touches the Mediterranean Sea.
Tunisia is between Africa and Europe,
close to Italy.
What is the capital city of Tunisia?
The capital city is Tunis.
Tunis is a busy city with markets,
mosques, cafes, and old buildings.
In Tunis, you can visit the Medina,
Old City, and the Bardo Museum.
It is the largest city in the country.
Other cities include Spax,
an important port city,
Seuss, a tourist city by the sea,
Kyrawan, a holy Islamic city,
Djerba, an island with beaches and culture.
How many people live in Tunisia?
About 12 million people live in Tunisia.
Many people live in cities,
but there are also villages,
desert towns, and farms.
What language do people speak in Tunisia?
The official language is Arabic.
People speak Tunisian Arabic in daily life.
Many people also speak French,
and some speak English or Berber in some regions.
Tunisian Arabic has words from French, Italian, and Turkish.
What is the weather like in Tunisia?
Tunisia has a Mediterranean climate in the North.
Hot, dry summers, mild, rainy winters.
In the South, it is desert, hot and dry all year.
It is a great place for sunshine and beach holidays.
What does Tunisia look like?
Tunisia has long beaches by the Mediterranean Sea,
Green Hills in the North,
the Sahara Desert in the South,
old ruins from the Roman Empire,
olive trees, date palms,
and sand dunes.
You can visit ancient cities like Carthage
and beautiful desert towns like Tazur.
What animals live in Tunisia?
In Tunisia, you can find camels,
goats, and sheep.
Foxes, jackals, and gazelles.
Birds like falcons, owls, and storks,
lizards, snakes, and scorpions in the desert.
In the sea, fish, octopus, and dolphins.
Camels are used for tourism and transport in the desert.
What do people eat in Tunisia?
Tunisian food is spicy, tasty,
and full of Mediterranean flavors.
People eat couscous,
the national dish with meat and vegetables,
bread, olives, and cheese,
lamb, chicken, and seafood,
chickpeas, beans, and tomatoes.
Popular dishes.
Brick, a thin-fried pastry with egg and tuna,
lob lobby, spicy chickpea soup,
oja, eggs cooked in tomato and pepper sauce,
harissa, a hot chili paste used in many foods.
What do people drink in Tunisia?
People drink water and mint tea.
Strong coffee, often sweet,
fresh juice, orange lemon, or pomegranate.
Adults may drink wine or beer,
especially in cities.
Tea is sometimes served with pine nuts in the glass.
What is life like in Tunisia?
Life in Tunisia is a mix of modern and traditional.
People enjoy spending time with family,
going to cafes and markets,
visiting the beach or countryside,
watching football and chatting with friends,
celebrating holidays with music and food.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, March 20th,
Republic Day, July 25th,
Eid al-Fetor and Eid al-Ada,
important Islamic holidays.
Ramadan, a holy month of fasting and prayer,
New Year and Christmas, celebrated by some families.
People wear traditional clothes during festivals and weddings.
Tunisian music and dance are part of many celebrations.
Some fun facts about Tunisia.
Tunisia was the home of ancient Carthage.
Star Wars movies were filmed in the Tunisian desert.
The flag is red and white with a crescent moon and star.
Tunisia has olive trees that are over 1,000 years old.
It is one of the most liberal countries in the Arab world.
Now you know many things about Tunisia.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the desert, the couscous and the sea.
Well done.
I am Emili.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Arabic, Maasalama.
